Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVIe DILG OPINION NO. 100 S. 2010 PUNONG BARANGAY LEO C. MOLINA Barangay Guintigbasan, Santa Fe Romblon Dear Punong Barangay Molina: This pertains to your letter seeking the Department's legal opinion on the following and we quote: "a) Is a Barangay Kagawad allowed to resign if she has a pending administrative case in the Sangguniang Bayan? b) Who is responsible for allowing a Barangay Kagawad to res ign? c) Is there a permanent vacancy in the Sanggunian if one of the 13arangay Kagawad resigned with a pending .administrative case? d) Are the remaining Sangguniang Barangay can have a session even if the (5) of the (7) Kagawad(s) are suspended?" In reply to your first and second queries, please be informed that the law does not prohibit any elective official to resign from office even if he/she has a pending administrative case in the Sangguniang Bayan, provided that the requirements under Section 82 of the Local Government Code had been complied with, thus: (a) "SEC. 82. Resignation of Elective Local Officials.- Resignation by elective local officials shall be deemed effective only upon acceptance by the following authorities: xxx xxx xxx

-2- (4) The city or municipal Jnayor, in the case of barangay officials.' In addition. we would like to invite your attention to the case of Ortiz vs. COMELEC (162 SCRA 812), where the Supreme Court defined resignation as the "act o/ giving up or the act OJ' an officer bl' which he declines his office and renounces the further right to use it. It is an expression of the incumbent in some form, express or implied, of the intention to surrender, renounce and relinquish the office and the acceptance by cmnpetent and lawful authority". In the case of Sangguniang Bayan Of San Andres Catanduanes vs. Court of Appeals (G.R. No. 11883, 16 January 1998), the Supreme Court held that "to constitute a complete and opera live resignation from office, there must be: (a) an intention to relinquish a part of the ternl,• (b) an act of relinquishment; and (c) an acceptance by the proper authority". Moreover, in Punzalan Y}. Mendoza (140 SCRA 153). the Supreme Court held implicit, but no less clearly, that the effectivity of a public official's resignation depends not on such much on its terms, e.g. "effective at the pleasure of the President", or at a particular tinw or on the happening of a particular contingency, but as a legal proposition, an acceptance thereof by the proper authority. For quite obviously, such appropriate authority can disregard the terms of the official's resignation, and as easily reject it as accept it ... (cited in Joson vs. Nario Ill, 187 SCRA 453). In view of the foregoing, it is clear that to be a valid resignation, the tender thereof must be in writing and must be accepted by the public officer authorized by law to accept the same. In this case, the resignation of the Barangay Kagawad (Sangguniang Barangay Member) shall be deemed effective only upon acceptance by the Municipal Mayor of Santa Fe, Romblon. As to the issue on who is responsible for allowing a Barangay Kagawad to resign, please be informed that since the law does not provide for a prohibition for any elective official with pending case to resign. the Municipal Mayor, who is authorized by law to accept the said resignation, is not liable for allowing the Barangay Kagawad, who has a pending case, to resign. However, the said Kagawad with pending case, who will resign from office, will not be allowed to receive his benefits pending resolution of his case. In reply to your third query, please be informed that Section 44 of the Local Government Code provides that "a permanent vacancy arises when an elective local official fills a higher vacant office, refuses to assume office,

-3- voluntarily resigns, or is otherwise perntanent incapacitated to discharge the functions of his office". In reply to your fourth query. please be informed that you have two options for which to remedy the temporary vacancy in your Sanggunian, to wit: I. By applying Supreme Court jurisprudence, the remaining Sangguniang Barangay Members may still transact official business or conduct session since quorum is effectively reduced as a result of the suspension of other members, or 2. In order to maintain as much as possible the widest representation in the Sangguniang Barangay, to request HEPGMA or the incoming President of the Philippines to appoint temporarily five individuals as Members of the Sangguniang Barangay in view of the power of the President to appoint "all other officers of the governnwnt whose appointments are not provided for by law" (Section 16, Article VII, 1987 Constitution). With regard to the first option, well-settled is the rule that the Sanggunian shall transact official business only when there is the presence, in a particular session, of at least a majority of all the members who have been elected and qualified. The majority shall constitute the so-called quorum under Section 53 (a) of the Local Government Code. In the case of Avelino vs. Cuenca (83 Phil. 17), the Supreme Court excluded a Member of the Senate in the determination of quorum in the sessions of the Senate since the excluded Senator was in the United States and. therefore, outside the coercive jurisdiction of the Senate. In effect, this situation would effectively reduce, for the time being, the quorum of the Senate. Applying this case law in your situation, the suspension ordered against the five Sangguniang Barangay Members would bring the concerned officials outside the coercive jurisdiction of the Sanggunian found in Section 53 (b) and (c) of the Local Government Code since their suspension would constitute a legal restriction for them to discharge their powers, duties and functions. We are of the view. therefore. that the remaining Sangguniang Barangay Members shall be the basis in determining your Sanggunian's quorum. As to the second option, if only to maintain the widest representation in the Sangguniang Barangay, you may instead submit a written request to the

-4- President of the Philippines to appoint temporarily the five regular members invoking thereof the power of the President of the Republic to appoint "all other officers of the government whose appointntents are not provided for by law" (Sec. 16, Art. VII. 1987 Constitution). The vacancy in your Sangguniang Barangay is of peculiar nature and no existing statute address this vacancy which thus warrants an extra-ordinary, but legal remedy. Hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: . JESUS DOQU IV Director Ill Legal: /La Director Rolando Calabazaron DILG Region tV-B Santos & Sons Bldg.. Aurora Blvd. Cubao. Quezon City The DILG Municipal Field Office Santa Fe. Romblon
